profile.summary: kswedberg is a mid-level JavaScript developer with deep expertise in jQuery's core internals, particularly its selector engine and animation system. Their contributions focus on debugging selector-related regressions, refining animation easing methods, and maintaining jQuery's test suite with QUnit. While their skills are primarily tied to jQuery's legacy JavaScript patterns (prototype-based OOP, callback-based async), they demonstrate strong debugging abilities and attention to documentation quality. The developer's experience is specialized in jQuery maintenance rather than modern JavaScript frameworks or backend systems.
skill_evidence: Fixed selector tests broken by QUnit commit (abfab1713ccb588aa87136b199a9ddc8d1b56c4b), demonstrating deep knowledge of jQuery's selector engine and interaction with QUnit's test framework
Addressed inconsistencies in easing shorthand methods for jQuery animations, showing expertise in the animation system's callback and timing mechanisms
Updated CONTRIBUTING.md to redirect Bug Patching Guide, indicating familiarity with jQuery's contribution processes and documentation structure
Referenced specific QUnit commit in PR discussion to trace regression, proving ability to debug cross-component issues in large codebases
Implemented fixes for :only-child and :last-child selectors, demonstrating practical understanding of CSS selector specificity and jQuery's implementation
Maintained test stability by ensuring selector tests passed after external QUnit changes, showcasing test suite maintenance skills
Contributed to documentation improvements that enhance developer onboarding for new jQuery contributors
Worked with jQuery's prototype-based method chaining patterns in animation system fixes, reflecting legacy JavaScript expertise
